# ADR-0004: All art generated by Blender Python, not hand-modelled

**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-09-17 · **Deciders:** engineering, art

## Context

Tonight needs a lot of art: building pieces in three materials with edit
variants, weapons across five classes and five rarities, harvestable props,
terrain modules, and POI kit pieces. There is no art team.

The project is also explicitly agent-driven over MCP. An agent can drive Blender
through the Blender MCP server, but "sculpt a compelling character" is not a
tractable agent task, whereas "emit a mesh from parameters" is.

Separately, hand-modelled assets are effectively un-reviewable in version
control. A `.blend` file is an opaque binary; a pull request that changes one is
a leap of faith.

## Decision

**Every mesh in Tonight is produced by a deterministic Python generator** under
`blender/scripts/`, built on a shared library at `blender/lib/tonight/`.

1. Generators run headless: `blender --background --python <script>`.
2. Generators are deterministic. Every random draw comes from
   `tonight.rng.seeded(name)`; the same inputs always produce the same mesh.
3. `.blend` files are **not** the source of truth and are not committed. The
   Python is the source of truth.
4. Exported FBX in `blender/exports/` is **gitignored** and regenerated. Binary
   build output does not belong in git.
5. The shared library must import **without `bpy`**, so it is unit-testable in
   ordinary CI with no Blender install. `bpy` usage is confined to
   `blender/scripts/` and a thin adapter layer.
6. Export always goes through `tonight.export.export_fbx()`, which owns the
   Blender-Z-up → Unity-Y-up conversion and the metric scale. Direct
   `bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx` calls are prohibited.

## Consequences

**We accept:**

- A hard ceiling on art quality. Scripts make clean, geometric, stylised
  shapes. They do not make sculpted organic detail. This is why "readable over
  realistic" is a pillar rather than a preference — the decisions reinforce each
  other, and if we ever want realism, this ADR is the blocker.
- Characters are the weakest case. A generated humanoid is a blocky proxy.
  Accepted through M6; a hand-authored character is the most likely future
  exception to this ADR, and it would need a new ADR to supersede this one.
- Generator authoring is a programming task, so art iteration needs a programmer.
  Mitigated by generators taking parameters from the same Blueprint-style data
  the game uses.
- Rig and animation are not covered by this ADR. Animation is deferred; when it
  lands it will most likely be authored, not generated.

**We gain:**

- Art that is diffable and reviewable — a change to a wall is a change to a
  readable Python function.
- Full regeneration from a clean checkout, which is an M0 exit criterion.
- Parametric variation for free: one wall generator produces wood, stone, and
  metal variants.
- A tractable MCP surface: an agent editing generator parameters is doing real
  art work.
- CI can assert mesh hashes and catch an unintended geometry change.

## Alternatives considered

**Buy asset packs.** Fastest to a good-looking prototype. Rejected: licensing
complexity for an open MIT repo, no parametric variation, and it removes the
agent-driven-art goal that motivates the MCP half of the project.

**Hand-model in Blender, commit `.blend`.** Rejected on reviewability and on the
absence of an art team.

**Generate in Unity with ProBuilder / C# mesh code.** Tempting — it removes
Blender from the loop entirely. Rejected because the brief specifies Blender, and
because Blender's modelling operators (bevel, solidify, boolean, UV unwrap) are
far more capable than anything reasonable to reimplement in C#.
